lina: Quick follow-up from the CP-split RFC — who owns route add/removes when we attach/detach peerings at scale? We hit some noisy churn on staging yesterday.

akshay: We saw ~240 route table modifications in 90s during a multi-tenant cutover, CloudWatch alarm fired. Noticed route propagation lag too.

sofia: Oof. Two orthogonal choices:
- push routes from control plane (we own RT updates per tenant)
- push routes from customer-side setup (customer NAT/relay creates routes locally)
Pros/cons: centralized = easier policy, centralized limits; distributed = fewer cross-account attachments but harder ops.

dave: AWS limits: peering attachments per account and route table propagation ops per RT are throttled. If we keep per-tenant peering we'll blow limits at scale.

lina: Another option: regional overlay relay (a small fleet in our VPCs) + SNAT per-tenant. That uses one peering per region and avoids route churn. But increases bandwidth egress per region and adds single-hop latency.

sofia: For private deployments the relay can't be in our VPC. Could do ephemeral tunnels from customer-private-agent -> regional relay. That reduces route churn but requires tunnel lifecycle management.

akshay: Practicality: if we go with "one peering per region + relay" we must solve cost accounting (which tenant used what bytes) and circuit-level failure modes.

infra-bot: ALERT: route-update-rate-limit-triggered — staging-route-rtb-02 (2025-03-15T16:02:14Z) :rate=257/min :action=throttle

dave: Also TLS termination question: do we terminate at relay or at endpoint? Terminating at relay lets us inspect/route but customer may require E2E TLS. If E2E, relays need passthrough with SNI proxying.

lina: Thinking tradeoffs matrix:
- Per-tenant peering: low latency, per-tenant isolation, route churn, peering limits
- Regional relay + single peering: low route churn, simpler peering, higher egress cost, possible multi-tenancy surface
- Ephemeral agent tunnels: private deploy friendly, more complexity in lifecycle

sofia: Quick spike suggestions:
1) simulate 1k tenants attach/detach in staging and measure RT updates and propagation time
2) prototype SNAT relay; measure added p50/p95 latency and bandwidth
3) design billing tags for bytes per tenant (vpc-flow + tagging)

akshay: I'll open a ticket with perf data and assign spike to "networking/spikes/route-churn". If we confirm route-thrash is real, prioritize relay spike.

lina: cool. @dave can you list exact peering/route quotas per region/account so we have thresholds? Also add security constraints for TLS/E2E.

dave: Will do, dropping numbers here by EOD. Also attaching a tiny terraform snippet I used to repro.

dave: ```
resource "aws_route" "to_relay" {
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.tenant_rt.id
  destination_cidr_block = "10.100.0.0/16"
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.relay.id
}
```

lina: Thanks. Action items: akshay spike + data, sofia relay prototype, dave quotas & snippet, I'll write the follow-up RFC PR with tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
